column2: nacio el VEINTE Y NUEVE DE MAYO del pasado ano CUARENTA Y TRES, hijo legitimo de *** AVELINO SERENA y AMBROSIA TRAIBEL ***. Paternos FRANCISCO y MARIA FERNANDEZ. Maternos JUAN e ISABEL CENTENO. *** Padrinos LUIS [L]ERENA y JUSTINIANA LENGUAS ***

column1: # *** EVERY ACT ON IT ENDS THE SAME WAY: *** "asi consta del LEGAJO conservado en este Archivo, mandado
# TRASLADAR por el Senor Obispo y Vicario Apostolico D. JACINTO VERA, de que doy fe." Not the Lerena
# entries - ALL of them, the Peraltas and Quirogas and Oteros too. This is not a parish register being
# kept. *** It is a bundle of loose papers being copied into a book, three years late, by order of the
# Bishop. *** The archive had already spotted the formula on two acts and reasoned about copies against
# originals. It is the whole page, and the whole page has one cause.
# *** THE CAUSE IS THE GUERRA GRANDE. *** Oribe's army closed on Montevideo in FEBRUARY 1843 and the
# siege ran nine years. These three Lerena children were born in FEBRUARY, MAY and JULY 1843 - the first
# of them in the very month the siege began - and none was christened until January 1846.
# *** AND WHERE THEY WERE CHRISTENED PLACES THE FAMILY. *** The Capilla de la Mauricia stood in the
# VILLA DE LA UNION - which Oribe renamed the VILLA RESTAURACION and made his seat, the government
# outside the walls, for the duration. The Lerenas were not inside besieged Montevideo. They were in
# ORIBE'S town, having their children baptised by ORIBE'S priest.
# *** WHICH SITS BESIDE SOMETHING THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY HELD AND HAD NOT JOINED UP: *** Luis Lerena's
# FIRST WIFE, married 3 September 1836, was CAROLINA ORIBE. And the 1850 baptism of his son Alberto
# Octavio is recorded at "S. Agustin, PUEBLO DE LA RESTAURACION" - the same place under Oribe's name,
# four years later.
# *** STATED AS WHAT IT IS. *** A family living in the Villa Restauracion through the siege, marrying an
# Oribe and baptising in Oribe's parish, was on the BLANCO side of the Guerra Grande. That is a reading
# of where they lived and whom they married, not a claim from any political record, and no relationship
# to Manuel Oribe is asserted - the archive has already had to withdraw a reading of this bride's
# surname once. See data/1836-luis-carolina-oribe.tsv.
# ================ *** AND A CONTRADICTION IN THE SOURCE *** ================
# Luis Eugenio: born *** 9 FEBRUARY 1843 ***. His sister Justiniana Mauricia: born *** 30 JULY 1843 ***.
# *** FIVE AND A HALF MONTHS, BETWEEN TWO FULL SIBLINGS. BOTH CANNOT BE RIGHT. ***
# Neither reading is a machine's: both acts have been read verbatim and both say "cuarenta y tres". The
# error is the 1846 clerk's, working from loose papers and writing "ano cuarenta y tres" three times on
# one page. A year carried forward from the entry above is the likeliest explanation AND IS A GUESS.
# Luis Eugenio's 1901 death registration gives an age; testing it against 1843 is the next step.
# *** THIS IS ALSO THE PAIR THE ARCHIVE'S OWN CONSISTENCY CHECKER WAS WRITTEN TO CATCH, AND DID NOT. ***
# The test read a structured parent field that 30 of 245 rows carry. See data/corrections.tsv.
